title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem 685 asks for the asymptotic number of distinct prime divisors of the binomial coefficient C(n,k) when n^ε < k ≤ n^{1-ε}. The conjectured answer is ω(C(n,k)) ~ k · Σ_{k<p<n} 1/p.
mathContext: Binomial coefficients encode rich arithmetic information. The prime factorization of C(n,k) reflects how primes in various ranges divide the product n(n-1)···(n-k+1)/k!. Primes p in (k,n) each divide C(n,k) exactly when ⌊n/p⌋ > ⌊k/p⌋ + ⌊(n-k)/p⌋, which happens with probability ~k/p by Kummer's theorem.

title: Prime Divisor Count ω(n)
content: **`omega n`** = `n.primeFactors.card`, the number of distinct prime divisors of n. This is the additive function ω, not the big-Ω that counts multiplicity.
mathContext: By the Hardy–Ramanujan theorem, ω(n) ~ log log n for typical n. For binomial coefficients, the prime divisor count can be much larger due to the product structure.

title: Prime Reciprocal Sum
content: **`primeSumInRange k n`** = Σ_{k<p<n, p prime} 1/p, the sum of prime reciprocals in the open interval (k, n).
mathContext: By Mertens' theorem, Σ_{p≤x} 1/p ~ log log x. So primeSumInRange(k,n) ~ log log n - log log k. When k = n^ε, this is ~ (1-ε) log log n, giving ω(C(n,k)) ~ k · (1-ε) log log n.

title: Main Conjecture
content: **Erdős Problem 685**: For n^ε < k ≤ n^{1-ε}, the number of distinct prime divisors of C(n,k) satisfies ω(C(n,k)) = (1+o(1)) · k · Σ_{k<p<n} 1/p. The formalization captures this as a (1±δ)-sandwich for any δ > 0 and all large n.
mathContext: The conjecture says that primes p ∈ (k,n) each independently divide C(n,k) with probability ~k/p, and the total count concentrates around its expectation. This is a concentration phenomenon for the additive function ω applied to a highly structured number.

title: Trivial Lower Bound
content: ω(C(n,k)) ≥ log C(n,k) / log n. Since each prime divisor is at most n, C(n,k) ≤ n^{ω(C(n,k))}.
mathContext: This bound is tight when k > n^{1-o(1)}, because then C(n,k) ~ n^k/k! and the prime factorization is dominated by small primes appearing with high multiplicity.

title: Tightness Near n
content: For k > n^{1-ε}, the trivial lower bound is asymptotically tight: ω(C(n,k)) ≤ (1+ε) · log C(n,k) / log n. This shows the conjecture's range restriction n^ε < k ≤ n^{1-ε} is necessary.

title: Verified Basic Properties
content: Three properties proved constructively: **ω(1) = 0** (1 has no prime divisors), **ω(C(n,0)) = 0** (since C(n,0) = 1), and **ω(C(n,1)) = ω(n)** (since C(n,1) = n). These are verified by Lean's kernel, not axiomatized.
mathContext: These boundary cases ground the formalization: the conjecture's interesting range starts at k ≥ 2 where the binomial coefficient has non-trivial factorization.

title: Characterization of ω = 0
content: ω(n) = 0 if and only if n ≤ 1. This axiom connects the prime divisor count to the structure of small numbers.
